articles.title: Xbox's First-Ever COO Is Already Leaving After A Few Months
articles.summary: Just a couple of months after being instated as Xbox's first-ever Chief Operating Officer, Helen Chiang has left the company. Her departure reinforces just how much of a whirlwind year 2026 has been for Xbox leadership, as the company continually attempts to reinvent itself before the start of the…
body: In the July 2026 Resetting Xbox post announcing 3,200 layoffs, new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma also revealed that Helen Chiang, who was previously Studio Head at Minecraft's Mojang was becoming COO of Xbox. Chiang had "end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services," with Sharma stating that Chiang would "will bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results."

Now, just over three months after that post, The Verge reports that Helen Chiang is leaving Xbox. In a short internal memo to Xbox developers, Sharma confirmed Chiang's departure, stating that she's "grateful for her years of service" and that Xbox will "share more on COO leadership as plans are finalized." Publicly, Xbox did not highlight her departure in the same way the spotlighted Phil Spencer's, with VP of Communications Kari Perez telling The Verge that "We don't discuss individual personal matters," and "We're grateful for Helen's years of service and wish her the best."
points: Just a couple of months after being instated as Xbox's first-ever Chief Operating Officer, Helen Chiang has left the company.
Her departure reinforces just how much of a whirlwind year 2026 has been for Xbox leadership, as the company continually attempts to reinvent itself before the start of the…

articles.title: Mass Effect Universe "looked incredible" says creator who claims he advised BioWare
articles.summary: A content creator who claims to have served on a BioWare community council has shared alleged details about the cancelled next Mass Effect game, titled Mass Effect Universe.
body: In a lengthy Twitter/X post (thanks, PC Gamer ), YouTuber Dantics claimed the cancelled game was set more than 600 years after the Reaper War.
He said he'd had access via his role on the "Mass Effect Council" and had seen firsthand what BioWare was developing, and provided feedback during development.

According to Dantics, the game would have centred on a "galactic Cold War" between three major factions, rather than another Reaper-style invasion. Humanity, the Krogan, the Batarians, and others would have allied, with the Council races forming their own alliance and the Geth emerging as a third superpower.
He also mentioned Geth-built megastructures, connections between the Milky Way and Andromeda, and a "shadowy adversary".
points: A content creator who claims to have served on a BioWare community council has shared alleged details about the cancelled next Mass Effect game, titled Mass Effect Universe.

articles.title: 'Wildwood' Is a "Risky" Movie — Just Like 'Coraline' Was 20 Years Ago
articles.summary: What was the last thing you did that took 16 years to accomplish? No shame — but director Travis Knight has a different level of persistence than most of us.
body: It took Knight and his stop-motion animation studio Laika nearly two decades to bring Wildwood, their latest film, to life. Even then, the studio behind Coraline wasn't entirely prepared for the challenges of its most ambitious movie yet. Knight (who yes, also directed an entire He-Man movie over the course of this journey) says the dark fantasy pushed his team to invent new technologies, rethink old techniques, and take the kinds of risks Hollywood studios tend to avoid.

Polygon spoke with Knight about the long road to Wildwood, the film's surprisingly complicated animated feats, and why he took a unique road to theaters despite years of working with the major studios.
WIldwood is a marvelous film, which took a long time to come together. You acquired the rights in 2010 — what were the bumps in the road?

articles.title: Aaron Paul Originally Had A Much More Important Role In Clayface
articles.summary: Clayface hit theaters this weekend, but one actor's role turned out to be smaller than expected. We knew Aaron Paul would be in the DC horror flick prior to its release, but in the final film, he cameos in just one scene.
body: Breaking Bad and Dispatch actor Aaron Paul appears during one of Clayface's most memorable sequences, as Matt Hagen transforms into him during a sequence set in Vesuvius to kill a Szabo gang member who killed his father. It turns out Aaron Paul was portraying Matt Hagen's abusive father, with Watkins telling Entertainment Weekly that Paul's character originally had more scenes in the movie.

"In terms of trying to figure out the character, it was, 'How much is Matt defined by his past, and how much is he an everyman?' At one point, we were looking at it and thinking, 'Is it the sins of the father?' But actually, as we worked on the script, I thought that notion of revenge was more universal and more relatable to all of us," Watkins revealed, highlighting how the central themes of the movie evolved in post-production.

"It doesn’t matter whether you’re carrying a trauma or any of that," he continued. "If we’re slighted, we carry this sense of being wronged, and we all want to do something, but generally in life we can’t do anything about it, and we’re powerless."
points: Clayface hit theaters this weekend, but one actor's role turned out to be smaller than expected.
We knew Aaron Paul would be in the DC horror flick prior to its release, but in the final film, he cameos in just one scene.

Now, the developer has removed several AI generated voice lines from the game, following a backlash to his use of the very technology which the game lampoons.

Pedercini—who also goes by Mollieindustria—received considerable support during that debacle. But the reaction to Future? No Thanks' AI use has been rather less supportive, prompting Pedercini to rework the game and respond to the backlash.

articles.title: Nintendo Is Still Being Wildly Underestimated
articles.summary: Switchboard is Polygon's weekly newsletter for all things Nintendo, sent on Thursdays and published on the site on Saturdays. You can subscribe here.
body: Nintendo has always enjoyed the respect of critics. The games, at their best, are just too good for things to be otherwise. It is total critical orthodoxy that Shigeru Miyamoto is one of the greatest and most influential game designers of all time, and that Mario and Zelda games are foundational texts of the video game medium that have successfully rewritten themselves and stayed relevant over time.

Yet there have been times throughout the company's history when Nintendo's image, and the audiences it has chosen to cultivate, have deflated this reputation. In the edgy late 1990s and early 2000s, when PlayStation ruled all, the family-friendliness and colorful styling of Nintendo games led to some people writing them off as kids' stuff. And when Nintendo sought out a new casual-gaming audience with the Wii and DS, some of its core fans felt betrayed, and couldn't find the depth or sophistication they wanted in the games.
points: Nintendo has always enjoyed the respect of critics.
The games, at their best, are just too good for things to be otherwise.

articles.title: Award-winning sci-fi author NK Jemisin joins BioWare's mourners and scorns a broken industry for killing geese that 'laid the golden eggs'
articles.summary: The death of BioWare has provoked a whole lot of tributes, memorialisation, and plain old nostalgia as all sorts of people come together to remember the bangers the erstwhile king of RPGs put out in its prime.
body: But the BioWare classics were big enough bangers to transcend videogames in their influence. Over on Bluesky, award-winning sci-fi and fantasy writer Nora Jemisin (better known as NK Jemisin) has been mourning the studio too.

"RIP Bioware. The [Mass Effect] and [Dragon Age] games were a literal inspiration, and I can't count how many times I've replayed my faves," Jemisin wrote. "I made lifelong friends on ME3 Multiplayer. I still think Jennifer Hepler is the best game writer I've seen, and Jennifer Hale's the best VA."

Hepler was a long-time Dragon Age writer who " was pretty much in charge of the dwarf origin story " in Origins, and also shaped much of the setting's dwarven culture in general. Jennifer Hale, meanwhile, is Jennifer Hale: Dynaheir, Mazzy Fentan, Bastila Shan, the female Commander Shepard, and plenty else. Many people, myself included, first became aware of Hale through her contributions to BioWare's RPGs.

articles.title: Xbox's first chief operating officer Helen Chiang leaves Microsoft just three months into the job
articles.summary: Helen Chiang, Xbox’s first-ever chief operating officer (COO), is leaving Microsoft just three months after taking the job.
body: According to The Verge, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed Chiang’s departure in an internal memo circulated on 23rd October.
"Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today. I'm grateful for her years of service and wish her well," Sharma wrote.

Sharma provided no details on why Chiang - who'd been at Microsoft for 21 years and had previously served as head of Minecraft - was leaving the company, only adding, "we'll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalised". It's thought her duties will be shared between other Xbox execs.

Sharma created the role in July as part of Xbox's massive "reset", saying it was needed to "work toward a shared goal, make the right tradeoffs, and get things done". It also came with 3200 layoffs and four studio departures in "most significant" Xbox restructuring in history.

articles.title: After 14 years of development, Factorio's final major update is out now
articles.summary: The whistle has blown. The belts have stopped. The furnace is silent and cold. After 14 years of continual development, Factorio has received its final major update. Developer Wube Software revealed that update 2.1 would be the last significant patch for its genre-defining factory building sim back…
body: If you were hoping Wube might sign off on Factorio on a similarly spectacular note, you may be disappointed. In its latest Friday Facts blog, the developer reiterates that 2.1 "isn't about new planets, enemies or research trees," and instead delivers "a big collection of quality of life, small features, polish, and the things we wanted to for 2.0 but didn't have time for."

This doesn't mean 2.1 has nothing of interest, however. Quite the opposite. The primary changes revolve around the space logistics introduced by Space Age, with Wube making it easier to ferry goods up into space and between planets. Rockets, for instance, can now carry multiple different items rather than just one thing, making it considerably easier to get space platforms built. On top of that, platforms can also transfer items between one another in orbit and automatically import items from all available locations.

Also on the space logistics front, Wube has added a constructable unloading bay that can be attached to landing pads, allowing inserters to pull out items and place them directly onto belts, into trains and so forth. This should make interplanetary logistics a bit easier.
points: After 14 years of continual development, Factorio has received its final major update.

articles.title: Star Wars Galaxies' Restoration project just received another massive update, including a huge visual upgrade and an overhaul to the Wookiees' home planet
articles.summary: I'm beginning to wonder whether Star Wars Galaxies Restoration can still be considered accurately named, given the community-driven revival project has gone so far beyond keeping SOE's 2003 MMO up and running.
body: Star Wars Galaxies Restoration: A New Dawn differs slightly from those previous updates. Where earlier patches have centred around one big new feature, A New Dawn is composed of various ideas suggested by members of the Restoration team. "We've expanded our team, adding 13 new team members to our project" the Restoration team wrote in a press release. "We asked everyone: work on something that they loved about Galaxies, and showcase that to the world."

This approach has produced an array of changes both large and small. The headline update is a game client upgrade that adds support for DirectX 12. This enables a bunch of snazzy graphical enhancements, including volumetric fog, clouds and atmosphere, a new water shader, greatly improved terrain distances, and support for upscaling tech like DLSS, FSR, and XeSS.

articles.summary: Spoilers follow for Clayface, which is now playing in theaters. Three-time Emmy winner Aaron Paul has a blink and you’ll miss it cameo in the new DC movie Clayface. Now, the film’s director, James Watkins, has revealed why the Breaking Bad and Westworld star is in DC’s first R-rated horror movie.
body: Paul plays Jimmy “One Nut” Hagen, the late abusive father of protagonist Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries). Word of Paul’s casting was first reported by Feature First back in June.

Paul’s cameo occurs during the climactic action sequence set at the Gotham City nightclub Vesuvius where Matt confronts the gangsters who disfigured him. Matt finds the hood who killed his dad and morphs into his father to shock the killer.

Paul originally had a larger supporting role in Clayface, appearing in flashbacks to Matt’s youth, but the filmmakers ultimately cut nearly all of those scenes. Paul’s appearance in the nightclub is all that remains of his role.
“In terms of trying to figure out the character, it was, How much is Matt defined by his past and how much is he an everyman?” Watkins told Entertainment Weekly.

articles.title: Dead by Daylight to Remove Chucky Content Just Months After Losing Michael Myers
articles.summary: Dead by Daylight fans are beside themselves after Behaviour Interactive announced that all Chucky content would no longer be available to purchase starting next month.
body: The developer behind the popular asymmetrical horror game confirmed plans to pull the Chucky Chapter from sale in posts shared across social media. The message followed rumors that the possessed killer doll would soon be removed from the game, with the official statement promising that those who have purchased related content will be able to use it even after it is removed from shelves starting November 24, 2026.

"We welcomed The Good Guy out of his box and into The Fog nearly three years ago, but it's now time for the Chucky Chapter to leave the shelf," Behaviour said. "On November 24, 2026, the Chapter and its associated content will be removed from in-game and first-party stores. Any content unlocked before that date will remain available to use in-game."

As detailed in an FAQ post shared by the developers, these changes to the Chucky Chapter mean a few things for Dead by Daylight players. Its Killer, known in-game as The Good Guy, will no longer be available to purchase, though bug fixes will still be supported. The collection of outfits and cosmetics he's gained since being added in 2023 will also be made unavailable, and no future add-ons for the character will be added.
